summary: Meta AI researcher Alexandr Wang announces the release of Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter agentic model with open weights under Apache 2.0 that runs on 24GB of VRAM, alongside a forthcoming open-weight version of Muse Spark 1.2.

mechanisms.reason: A stated VRAM figure for a 30B model implies a reduced hardware/memory footprint per unit of serving capability.
mechanisms.quote: muse glimmer can run on 24GB of VRAM without losing agentic reliability.

mechanisms.reason: A 30B model fitting in 24GB VRAM is deployable on single consumer/workstation GPUs rather than requiring datacentre-scale serving.
mechanisms.quote: muse glimmer can run on 24GB of VRAM without losing agentic reliability.

practices.reason: An engineering team could self-host or fine-tune a 30B agentic model released under a permissive license with a stated low memory footprint.
practices.quote: we also are releasing muse glimmer, a 30B agentic model with open weights under apache 2.0. muse glimmer can run on 24GB of VRAM without losing agentic reliability.

practices.reason: The claim that a 30B model runs on 24GB VRAM without losing agentic reliability suggests a serving efficiency worth investigating, though the technique behind it is unspecified.
practices.quote: muse glimmer can run on 24GB of VRAM without losing agentic reliability.

notable_reason: A concrete open-weight release of a 30B agentic model with a permissive license and stated low VRAM footprint is a specific, actionable event for teams evaluating self-hostable models.
